title: Fix silent speakers on 12-inch MacBook (CS4208)
author: teomurgi
body:
## Problem

On the 12-inch MacBook (MacBook9,1 / MacBook10,1) the internal speakers are completely silent out of the box. Headphones work; every mixer looks fine; PipeWire shows an active sink — and nothing comes out. `manual/44-mac-support.md` currently lists "Sound is not functioning" as a known Mac limitation.

Additionally, once speakers do work, **audio dies after every suspend/resume** and only a reboot brings it back.

## Root cause

The Cirrus Logic CS4208 codec's speaker amplifier is never powered by the in-tree driver: the HDA controller reports a **generic PCI subsystem ID** (`8086:7270`), so `snd_hda_codec_cs420x` matches no Apple fixup and probes with `speaker_outs=0` (only the headphone jack `0x10` is wired through the analog DAC). Mainline has no working speaker config for this codec.

Four independent things are required for sound to actually come out — and stay out:

1. **The out-of-tree driver** — [leifliddy/macbook12-audio-driver](https://github.com/leifliddy/macbook12-audio-driver) replays the codec init (reverse-engineered from macOS) that powers the amp.
2. **The EFI startup chime un-muted** in NVRAM. The firmware only energises the class-D speaker amp when it plays the boot chime; if the chime is muted the amp is never powered and no software fix can work.
3. **Software volume** — the speaker path has no hardware amp volume (the codec's only analog amp is on the headphone path), so without a WirePlumber soft-mixer rule the volume slider does nothing.
4. **Suspend pinned to the freeze path** — s2idle kills the speaker amp (see "Suspend" below).

## Fix

Detect the two models and install all four pieces:

| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| `install/hardware/apple/fix-macbook12-audio.sh` | Gates on `MacBook9,1\|MacBook10,1`; clones + DKMS-builds the driver; installs the WirePlumber soft-mixer rule; clears the chime mute bit; installs a `sleep.conf.d` drop-in pinning suspend to freeze |
| `install/hardware/all.sh` | Runs the fix during hardware setup |
| `migrations/<ts>.sh` | Applies the same fix to existing installs (idempotent; removes the superseded d3cold service if present; sets `reboot-required`) |
| `test/shell.d/macbook12-audio-test.sh` | 14 tests, all passing |
| `manual/44-mac-support.md` | Documents the fix, the expected chime, and software volume |

## Suspend: what actually works (tested)

The obvious fix — pinning the codec out of D3cold, mirroring `fix-suspend-nvme.sh` — was implemented first and **disproven on real hardware**:

- With `d3cold_allowed=0` confirmed active at runtime, suspend/resume still killed the speakers. Post-resume codec state looked fully alive (stream attached, GPIO amp lines up, D0 power) yet no output.
- A codec reinit attempt (`echo 1 > /sys/class/sound/hwC0D0/reconfig`) was refused — PipeWire holds the device.

What works: writing `freeze` to `/sys/power/state` keeps the amp alive across suspend — audio verified working after resume. These machines have no S3 (the kernel rejects `freeze` for `/sys/power/mem_sleep`), so the drop-in sets:

```ini
[Sleep]
SuspendState=freeze
MemorySleepMode=
```

The empty `MemorySleepMode=` forces systemd (≥254) onto the plain-freeze path instead of probing `mem_sleep`. Verified end-to-end: `systemctl suspend` → wake → speakers work.

## Notes

- **The chime write** must be a single `write()` on an `O_WRONLY` fd — piping through `tee` fails with `Invalid argument` (`tee` uses `O_TRUNC` and the firmware attribute word is rejected). The migration and install script both use that form.
- **Packaging tradeoff:** the driver is installed by cloning and building against the running kernel (same template as PR #11620 for the CS8409). That runtime build downloads the matching kernel source tarball from kernel.org (~140 MB) at DKMS build time. If you'd rather host a `macbook12-audio-driver-dkms` package in the omarchy repo, the script collapses to a single `omarchy-pkg-add` — happy to switch.

## Tested

Verified end-to-end on a MacBook10,1 running Omarchy 4.0.4 / kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy: before the fix the sink ran at 91% with `speaker_outs=0` and silence; after it the DKMS `snd_hda_codec_cs420x` loads from `updates/dkms/`, the chime is audible at boot, the internal speakers produce sound with working software volume, and audio survives suspend with the freeze drop-in. `./test/shell` passes (6 unrelated pre-existing environment failures, unchanged with this commit stashed).

Refs #11619 (MacBook audio, CS8409) and #12217 (CS4208 woofers on MacBookPro12,1) — same class of model-gated hardware fix.
